items.prompt: Explain how infrastructure can influence the proposed location and production decision. A government wants useful production in an area with weak transport links. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Government can influence business location, production and relationships between firms to pursue employment, development, environmental protection and fair competition. General tools include planning conditions, infrastructure, information, incentives and rules against harmful conduct. Explain why a problem needs attention and how the selected tool changes decisions. A location grant can reduce a site’s cost but cannot supply missing skills or customers by itself. Production standards can protect others but require implementation. Competition measures can address harmful agreements or market power without implying that every large firm is abusive. Improving access can remove a practical obstacle for firms and workers. An unrelated promotional slogan would not change delivery reliability.
marking_guidance: Starting point: Government can influence business location, production and relationships between firms to pursue employment, development, environmental protection and fair competition.

items.prompt: Explain how serviced local premises can address access and neighbour effects. A town offers serviced workshop space away from homes but connected to delivery roads. [6]
items.canonical_answer: At local level, public authorities can influence suitable land use, access, infrastructure and effects on neighbouring users. A business site needs to fit practical production and community requirements. Conditions or suitable industrial areas can reduce conflict, but a low-cost designated site is not automatically useful if customers, skills or utilities are inaccessible. The arrangement can reduce neighbouring disturbance and give firms usable access. Compare it with an isolated site rather than consider land price alone.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: At local level, public authorities can influence suitable land use, access, infrastructure and effects on neighbouring users.

items.prompt: Explain why national infrastructure can affect regional production choices. A national programme improves transport to an underserved production area. [6]
items.canonical_answer: National policy may seek more balanced regional development, employment and infrastructure. Assistance can influence firms’ site costs or access to skills and transport, but the investment must still be viable. A project that moves solely for a short subsidy may not remain once support ends. Assess durable capability and demand as well as initial incentives. Reliable access may help firms supply customers and workers reach jobs, creating a more lasting benefit than a one-time incentive without infrastructure.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: National policy may seek more balanced regional development, employment and infrastructure.

items.prompt: Explain how infrastructure and access can influence an international site comparison. An investor compares a serviced Namibian site with a foreign location offering cheap rent but unreliable delivery. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Government can influence international location through the general investment environment, infrastructure, trade relationships and eligible assistance. Firms compare market access, skills, reliability and total costs across sites. Incentives have costs and conditions, so they should not be treated as guaranteed or as the sole reason a foreign operation is worthwhile. Public investment in usable infrastructure can influence the choice, while rent alone does not establish competitiveness. Actual conditions and customer needs remain decisive.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Government can influence international location through the general investment environment, infrastructure, trade relationships and eligible assistance.

items.prompt: Explain how a production condition and capability support can serve different purposes. A producer can meet an environmental condition by installing effective control, while its staff need relevant skills. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Government can influence production through general safety, quality or environmental conditions and through support for skills, technology or infrastructure. Standards seek to protect affected people or maintain acceptable output; assistance seeks to remove capability constraints. Both require resources and monitoring. Do not assume every restriction is harmful or every grant improves productivity. A combination of a clear condition and appropriate capability support may secure production with less harm. Giving money without checking its use may fail to achieve that result.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Government can influence production through general safety, quality or environmental conditions and through support for skills, technology or infrastructure.

items.prompt: Explain why coordinated supply restriction can prompt government attention. In a market, suppliers agree to restrict supply together to raise the price faced by customers. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Government may act to support fair competition and address harmful collusion such as price-fixing, misuse of market power, mergers and takeovers that would remove competition, or practices that disadvantage others. The purpose can be to protect choice and fair opportunities rather than protect every competitor from any loss. Competition itself can press firms to improve. Evaluate the stated conduct and its effects instead of assuming any large enterprise or price reduction is abusive. Scrutiny of the agreement addresses coordinated restriction rather than mere successful competition. A small rival’s complaint alone would not prove the same conduct.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Government may act to support fair competition and address harmful collusion such as price-fixing, misuse of market power, mergers and takeovers that would remove competition, or practices that disadvantage others.

items.prompt: Explain why assistance should match Omi’s information and delivery constraint. Omi Crafts has good products but lacks reliable information about nearby regional buyers and delivery options. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Government can assist regional development, small firms and exports through grants, subsidies, tax allowances, low-interest loans, cheap or serviced premises, infrastructure, advice, training and information about markets. Regional support may address uneven opportunities; small firms may lack information or collateral; exporters may face unfamiliar customers and procedures. Assistance has an opportunity cost and can support weak projects if poorly targeted. Identify the actual constraint and conditions rather than assume a subsidy guarantees survival. Training may be on-the-job or off-the-job; choose it to address a capability gap rather than substitute for absent demand. Relevant market and logistics advice may address its gap more directly than an unneeded machine grant. The firm must still confirm demand and affordability.
marking_guidance: Starting point: Government can assist regional development, small firms and exports through grants, subsidies, tax allowances, low-interest loans, cheap or serviced premises, infrastructure, advice, training and information about markets.

items.prompt: Explain why regional assistance should address the missing electricity connection. A region has willing workers and demand access but lacks a reliable industrial electricity connection. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Regional assistance supports areas with limited economic opportunities through suitable infrastructure, advice, skills or conditional financial support. It can encourage productive activity and employment, but needs a realistic reason firms can operate there. Public cost and the risk of temporary relocation matter. Measure enduring outcomes rather than buildings or grant totals alone. Improving that connection can remove a stated obstacle. A marketing campaign about the region would not supply the missing utility.

items.prompt: Explain how advice can support Eya’s actual small-business constraint. Eya Repairs has customers and skills but weak cash planning. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Small firms can face limited finance, management time, information and access to specialist support. Match it to the specific weakness and check whether demand and operations are viable. Support does not eliminate business risk or establish a right to indefinite subsidy. Practical financial-planning advice can help identify payment timing and avoid an unaffordable commitment. An unrelated equipment grant may not address the problem.

items.prompt: Explain how targeted information can help Ota assess an export opportunity. Ota Crafts considers a nearby regional market but does not know buyer requirements or delivery costs. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Government helps exporters because exports earn foreign currency that pays for imports, create jobs, and raise tax revenue from exporters’ profits. It can help by offering low-interest loans, subsidies or tax reductions to exporters, insuring exporters against foreign buyers who do not pay, organising trade fairs and trade missions abroad, providing market information and advice about foreign requirements, and trying to keep the exchange rate stable. It can reduce information barriers but cannot guarantee foreign orders or remove all transport and payment risk. Exporting services may involve different access and delivery arrangements from sending physical goods. Confirm the opportunity and costs before committing. Market and logistics information helps assess suitability. A large export target without those details would be a weak basis for investment.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Government helps exporters because exports earn foreign currency that pays for imports, create jobs, and raise tax revenue from exporters’ profits. It can help by offering low-interest loans, subsidies or tax reductions to exporters, insuring exporters against foreign buyers who do not pay, organising trade fairs and trade missions abroad, providing market information and advice about foreign requirements, and trying to keep the exchange rate stable.

items.prompt: Evaluate whether a machine grant addresses Hela’s stated production constraint. A scheme offers machines to Hela Foods, but its existing equipment has spare capacity and its main problem is unreliable transport to customers. [8]
items.canonical_answer: Evaluate an intervention by linking its objective, mechanism, beneficiaries, resource cost and possible unintended effects. A grant may make useful investment possible but also use public funds that could support another need. Support may be temporary while an underlying weakness persists. Compare plausible alternatives such as information, infrastructure or a targeted capability improvement. Ask whether the measure actually changes the constraint and whether outcomes can be reviewed. Do not judge success from the amount spent or the number of applications alone. Extra machines may add idle capacity without improving delivery. Targeted logistics support may be more relevant, subject to cost and evidence. Choose the intervention addressing access first rather than rewarding investment for its own sake.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Evaluate an intervention by linking its objective, mechanism, beneficiaries, resource cost and possible unintended effects.

items.prompt: Evaluate the potential benefits and competitive risks of SADC membership for Namibia using Nela’s example. Nela Panels in Namibia considers a regional market where its product qualifies for the relevant preference. Customers still require reliable delivery and competitive quality. [8]
items.canonical_answer: Namibia is a member of the Southern African Development Community, SADC. Regional cooperation and trading arrangements can improve access to markets, inputs and shared infrastructure. Preferential treatment depends on applicable conditions; regional membership does not mean every product and service faces no barrier. Goods must meet rules-of-origin requirements to qualify for regional preferences. Wider market access can support sales and choice, but Namibian producers also face stronger competition. Benefits depend on competitiveness, logistics, quality and actual demand, while adjustment can impose costs on some firms and workers. Namibia also belongs to the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) with South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho and Eswatini: goods move between members largely free of customs duties, and members charge a common tariff on imports from outside. SADC is a wider regional community; the two organisations are not interchangeable. Regional access is an opportunity, not a guaranteed order. Preferential treatment can improve its position while rivals gain access too. Use the opportunity if product, delivered cost and capacity fit actual buyers, and assess adjustment risks rather than assume membership benefits all firms equally.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Namibia is a member of the Southern African Development Community, SADC.
